steps.observation: Work on this for 10 seconds; do not stop early. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Here are the key differences between DNA and RNA:

1. Sugar Backbone  
   • DNA contains deoxyribose (lacking one oxygen atom).  
   • RNA contains ribose (has one more oxygen).

2. Strandedness  
   • DNA is typically double-stranded, forming the familiar double helix.  
   • RNA is usually single-stranded and can fold into complex shapes.

3. Nitrogenous Bases  
   • DNA uses adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), and thymine (T).  
   • RNA uses A, G, C, and uracil (U) in place of thymine.

4. Location and Stability  
   • DNA is housed primarily in the cell nucleus (and mitochondria/chloroplasts). It is chemically more stable for long-term genetic storage.  
   • RNA is found in the nucleus and cytoplasm. It’s less stable (more prone to degradation), fitting its roles in “on-the-fly” tasks.

5. Primary Functions  
   • DNA stores and transmits hereditary information.  
   • RNA plays various roles in expressing that information:  
     – mRNA (messenger RNA) carries coding instructions to ribosomes.  
     – rRNA (ribosomal RNA) and tRNA (transfer RNA) help build proteins.  
     – Other RNAs regulate gene expression or modify other RNAs.

In short, DNA is the stable genetic blueprint, while RNA is the more transient molecule that reads, conveys, and helps execute those genetic instructions.
